changes.reason: Replace repeated ICNN induction formulas with closure-rule proof; retain convexity calculation and first/output cases.
changes.after:
\begin{proof}
Non-negative linear combinations plus constants preserve convexity. So does composition with a convex non-decreasing scalar function $\varphi$: for convex $u$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$,
\[
\varphi\bigl(u(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\bigr)
\le\varphi\bigl(\lambda u(x)+(1-\lambda)u(y)\bigr)
\le\lambda\varphi(u(x))+(1-\lambda)\varphi(u(y)).
\]
The first inequality uses convexity of $u$ and monotonicity of $\varphi$; the second uses convexity of $\varphi$. Starting from the affine $\preactl{1}$, these two closure rules give convex coordinates at every layer by induction, including the affine output.
\end{proof}

changes.reason: Remove repeated implication/expressivity explanation, preserve all distinctions and reference scope.
changes.before: If, in addition, $\Wl{1} \ge 0$ in Definition~\ref{def:icnn}, the network is simultaneously monotone and input-convex, hence non-decreasing \emph{and} convex by Propositions~\ref{prop:monotone_represents} and \ref{prop:icnn_convex}. Both $\relu$ and Maxout (below) are convex and monotone, so non-negative-weight \ac{relu} networks are of exactly this type. These are the building blocks of the DC splitting of Section~\ref{sec:dc_splitting_relu}: the streams $g$ and $h$ are computed by monotone networks acting on a signed embedding of the input, and are input-convex in the original input. The sign constraint also \emph{limits} expressivity---a weight-constrained \ac{relu} network represents only convex functions, precisely Proposition~\ref{prop:icnn_convex}, which is why monotone architectures add concave counterparts of the activation \parencite{Runje_2023}. The decompositions of this thesis turn the limitation into a feature: the difference of two such networks recovers full generality by Theorem~\ref{thm:cpwl_relu_equivalence} and \eqref{eq:cpwl_dc_representation}.
changes.after: With $\Wl{1}\ge0$, an \ac{icnn} is both monotone and convex by Propositions~\ref{prop:monotone_represents} and~\ref{prop:icnn_convex}. ReLU and Maxout meet both activation conditions. Section~\ref{sec:dc_splitting_relu} therefore constructs $g,h$ as monotone networks on a signed input embedding, convex in the original input. Non-negative-weight ReLU networks represent only convex functions; broader monotone architectures add concave activation counterparts \parencite{Runje_2023}. Taking differences instead recovers every \ac{cpwl} function by Theorem~\ref{thm:cpwl_relu_equivalence} and~\eqref{eq:cpwl_dc_representation}.

changes.before: \item \textbf{States.} For every hidden layer $l \in \{1, \ldots, L-1\}$, every neuron $i \in [d^{(l)}]$, and every turn label $q \in \{+,-\}$ there is an \emph{activation state} $s^{(l)}_{i,q}$, controlled by player $P^{q}$, so that $S_q = \bigl\{ s^{(l)}_{i,q} : l \in [L-1],\, i \in [d^{(l)}] \bigr\}$. For every input coordinate $k \in [d^{(0)}]$ and every $q \in \{+,-\}$ there is a \emph{terminal state} $s^{(0)}_{k,q}$, and there is one absorbing \emph{cemetery state} $\perp$ with zero payoff. Finally, there is a single \emph{output state} $s^{(L)}$ at the affine output neuron, at which no decision is taken.
changes.after: \item \textbf{States.} Each hidden neuron $i\in[d^{(l)}]$, $l\in[L-1]$, has activation states $s^{(l)}_{i,q}$ controlled by $P^q$, $q\in\{+,-\}$. The affine output state $s^{(L)}$ is assigned to $P^+$ with no choice of action. Terminal states are $s^{(0)}_{k,q}$ for $k\in[d^{(0)}]$, $q\in\{+,-\}$, and a zero-payoff \emph{cemetery} $\perp$; play ends upon reaching any terminal state.

changes.reason: Remove repeated acyclicity explanation and specify exact sign-selected edge identity instead of overbroad absolute-weight statement.
changes.before: The game graph is layered and acyclic---every transition strictly decreases the layer index or ends in the cemetery---so Theorem~\ref{thm:shapley_bellman} applies despite the discounts $\gamma^{(l)}_i$ being arbitrary positive numbers. Normalization and discounting cancel: the product of the transition probability \eqref{eq:rng_kernel} and the discount $\gamma^{(l)}_i$ is exactly the absolute weight $\abs{\Wl{l}_{ij}}$, so the Shapley--Bellman recursion reproduces the affine algebra of the forward pass.
changes.after: Each transition decreases the layer index or terminates, so Theorem~\ref{thm:shapley_bellman} applies for arbitrary positive structural discounts. Multiplying \eqref{eq:rng_kernel} by $\gamma^{(l)}_i$ restores the sign-selected weight $\Wsig{l}{q\oplus r}_{ij}$; summing signed successor values recovers the forward affine calculation.
